entries.name: NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3
entries.description: The built-in engine. 25 European languages, punctuation + casing, word timestamps; the only model with a Qualcomm NPU path.

measurements.machine: ASUS Zenbook A16 - Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme X2E94100, 48 GB, Windows 11 build 28000 ARM64
measurements.source: `lw bench tests/fixtures/audio --model-dir <models>/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 --backend cpu`, 2026-09-18, lw-cli built with --features sherpa (sherpa-onnx 1.13.6, greedy search, 8 threads, bundled ONNX Runtime CPU provider). Word-weighted WER 0.054 and mean RTF 0.0347 over 12 clip(s) in en/es/ru/uk. ONE SWEEP: every entry in this catalog was measured back to back on the CPU on this date, over the same committed twelve-clip fixture set, so the figures are comparable with each other. The CPU is the only accelerator they can all use -- sherpa-onnx links its own static ONNX Runtime with the CPU provider, so nothing but parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 has any other path. All twelve fixture clips, three per language.

measurements.machine: ASUS Zenbook A16 - Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme X2E94100, 48 GB, Windows 11 build 28000 ARM64
measurements.source: docs/benchmarks.md 5.1 - `lw bench tests/fixtures/audio --backend npu`, encoder on Hexagon HTP V81, 12 FLEURS clips, 2026-08-26

entries.notes: MEASURED on this project's target machine (Snapdragon X2 Elite X2E94100): end-to-end RTF 0.032 on the CPU EP and 0.0145 with the encoder on the Hexagon HTP V81, word-weighted WER 5.4% / 4.8% over 12 FLEURS clips - see docs/benchmarks.md 5.1. The per-language wer_estimates come from the same run with only 3 clips per language, so treat them as indicative, not statistically meaningful; the English figure is dominated by FLEURS number-word and casing normalisation ('2' vs 'two'), not misrecognition. download_bytes/disk_bytes are the exact pinned file sizes in models/manifests/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3.json and cover the CPU int8 artifact set, which is the only hash-pinned target today. The NPU path additionally needs a static-shape encoder and builds a ~1.2 GB HTP context binary locally on first use (~106 s, cached thereafter) - that is generated on the machine, not downloaded, and is not counted in disk_bytes. GPU: the same file also runs on a GPU through ONNX Runtime's WebGPU provider - no separate artifact and no extra download - measured on the X2's integrated Adreno at RTF 0.0862, WER 4.8% over the same 12 clips. The hardware field below lists artifact targets (which pinned file sets exist), not every provider that can run them.

entries.name: NVIDIA Parakeet TDT-CTC 110M en (transducer branch, sherpa-onnx export)
entries.description: The small English Parakeet: 110M parameters against the 600M of v2/v3, with punctuation and casing, at a fifth of the compute.

measurements.machine: ASUS Zenbook A16 - Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme X2E94100, 48 GB, Windows 11 build 28000 ARM64
measurements.source: `lw bench tests/fixtures/audio --model-dir <models>/parakeet-tdt-ctc-110m-en --backend cpu --languages en`, 2026-09-18, lw-cli built with --features sherpa (sherpa-onnx 1.13.6, greedy search, 8 threads, bundled ONNX Runtime CPU provider). Word-weighted WER 0.062 and mean RTF 0.0095 over 3 clip(s) in en. ONE SWEEP: every entry in this catalog was measured back to back on the CPU on this date, over the same committed twelve-clip fixture set, so the figures are comparable with each other. The CPU is the only accelerator they can all use -- sherpa-onnx links its own static ONNX Runtime with the CPU provider, so nothing but parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 has any other path. Three clips is indicative, not statistically meaningful, and must NOT be compared with the twelve-clip multilingual totals in this catalog.

entries.notes: VERIFIED: download_bytes/disk_bytes are the exact sum of the pinned file sizes in models/manifests/parakeet-tdt-ctc-110m-en.json, and every SHA-256 there was computed locally on 2026-09-16 from the bytes actually downloaded - upstream publishes no checksum for any of these files. disk_bytes equals download_bytes because the installer writes the files verbatim, with no archive to expand. SOURCE: the k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx `asr-models` GitHub release ships this model only as a .tar.bz2 archive and ModelDownloader cannot unpack archives, so the manifest pins the identical loose files from the sherpa-onnx author's Hugging Face mirror at a fixed commit revision. LICENCE: CC-BY-4.0, declared on the upstream model card nvidia/parakeet-tdt_ctc-110m. MEASURED on this project's target machine, 2026-09-16 - read the measurement's source line before quoting it. WHY A LANGUAGE SUBSET: `lw bench` scores only the clips in languages the engine claims, but lw-engine-sherpa reports a whole-family language list for offline transducers (the 25 European languages of the multilingual NeMo releases), which this monolingual export does not speak. Left to the full 12-clip set it would have been scored against Spanish, Russian and Ukrainian as well, producing a WER that describes nothing. So the run used a copy of tests/fixtures/audio holding only the English clips and their fixtures.json entries; the audio and the reference transcripts are the repository's own, unmodified. WHAT IT IS: NVIDIA's parakeet-tdt_ctc-110m is a hybrid trained with both a TDT-transducer and a CTC head on 36k hours of English; sherpa-onnx's conversion script (scripts/nemo/fast-conformer-hybrid-transducer-ctc/run-transducer-non-streaming.sh) exports the transducer branch, which is what is pinned here. It keeps punctuation and casing, like the 0.6B Parakeets. FULL PRECISION, NOT INT8: this is the one new entry whose artifact target is `any` rather than `cpu_int8`, because the matching csukuangfj/sherpa-onnx-nemo-parakeet_tdt_transducer_110m-en-36000-int8 repository is empty apart from .gitattributes - the quantized files exist only inside the .tar.bz2 on the GitHub release, which the installer cannot unpack. That is why a 110M-parameter model costs 455 MiB to download while the 600M parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2-en int8 costs 631 MiB. wer_estimates is empty: NVIDIA publishes figures for its own NeMo checkpoint, not for this ONNX export. Quality and speed tiers are EDITORIAL; 'better' rather than 'best' places it below the 0.6B Parakeets on parameter count. The engine string is `nemo_transducer`, as on parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v2-en. In this catalog that string means 'the sherpa-onnx offline transducer loader' - the encoder/decoder/joiner/tokens.txt layout - not a claim about who trained the weights. It is deliberately not `parakeet_tdt`: the built-in parakeet_tdt engine only loads the istupakov file layout (nemo128.onnx + vocab.txt + a fused decoder_joint graph) and cannot read this triple, so labelling it parakeet_tdt would promise a path that does not exist. Needs the `sherpa` engine feature.

entries.name: Whisper large-v3-turbo (sherpa-onnx export)
entries.description: OpenAI's large-v3 encoder with a 4-layer decoder: the lowest WER measured on this project's 12-clip fixture set, at about a third of medium's cost.

measurements.machine: ASUS Zenbook A16 - Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme X2E94100, 48 GB, Windows 11 build 28000 ARM64
measurements.source: `lw bench tests/fixtures/audio --model-dir <models>/whisper-turbo --backend cpu`, 2026-09-18, lw-cli built with --features sherpa (sherpa-onnx 1.13.6, greedy search, 8 threads, bundled ONNX Runtime CPU provider). Word-weighted WER 0.042 and mean RTF 0.1986 over 12 clip(s) in en/es/ru/uk. ONE SWEEP: every entry in this catalog was measured back to back on the CPU on this date, over the same committed twelve-clip fixture set, so the figures are comparable with each other. The CPU is the only accelerator they can all use -- sherpa-onnx links its own static ONNX Runtime with the CPU provider, so nothing but parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 has any other path. All twelve fixture clips, three per language. SUPERSEDES an RTF of 0.469 recorded on 2026-09-16 for the same model on the same machine. The accuracy reproduced exactly (0.042); the speed did not, and the earlier figure was taken outside this sweep under conditions that were not recorded. The number here is the one measured under the conditions stated above.

entries.notes: VERIFIED: download_bytes/disk_bytes are the exact sum of the pinned file sizes in models/manifests/whisper-turbo.json, and every SHA-256 there was computed locally on 2026-09-16 from the bytes actually downloaded - upstream publishes no checksum for any of these files. disk_bytes equals download_bytes because the installer writes the files verbatim, with no archive to expand. SOURCE: the k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx `asr-models` GitHub release ships this model only as a .tar.bz2 archive and ModelDownloader cannot unpack archives, so the manifest pins the identical loose files from the sherpa-onnx author's Hugging Face mirror at a fixed commit revision. MEASURED on this project's target machine, 2026-09-16: WER 0.042 over the same 12 clips on which whisper-medium scored 0.054 and parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 scored 0.054, at RTF 0.469 against medium's 1.250. On this fixture set that is the best accuracy-per-second of any Whisper entry here, but 12 clips cannot settle an ordering - read the source line before quoting it. wer_estimates stays empty for the usual reason: OpenAI's published figures describe the full-precision checkpoint, not this int8 export. Quality and speed tiers are EDITORIAL. WHAT TURBO IS: large-v3's encoder with the decoder cut from 32 layers to 4 - not a smaller, weaker large, but large-v3's acoustic model with a cheap decoder; OpenAI documents it as degrading on some languages relative to large-v3 itself. The language list is therefore large-v3's: openai/whisper tokenizer.py LANGUAGES plus 'yue', which large-v3 is the first size to support and which turbo inherits with the same tokenizer. Only the int8 encoder/decoder pair is pinned; the full-precision graphs sit in the same upstream repository and would cost several times the download for a quality difference nobody here has measured. LICENCE NOTE: recorded as MIT, the licence of the openai/whisper repository whose original checkpoints sherpa-onnx's export script downloads and converts; the `openai/whisper-*` model cards on Hugging Face declare apache-2.0 instead, so read both before redistributing. Needs the `sherpa` engine feature.

entries.name: GigaAM v3 Russian, with punctuation (int8 encoder, sherpa-onnx export)
entries.description: Russian-only Conformer transducer from Sber's GigaChat team, exported for sherpa-onnx with punctuation and text normalisation built in.
entries.notes: MEASURED on this project's target machine, 2026-09-17: WER 0.029 at RTF 0.0175 over the three Russian FLEURS fixtures, against parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3's 0.059 on the same three clips - twice the accuracy at roughly half the real-time factor, in a third of the download. VERIFIED: download_bytes/disk_bytes are the exact sum of the pinned file sizes in models/manifests/gigaam-v3-ru.json, and every SHA-256 there was computed locally from the bytes actually downloaded - upstream publishes no checksum. LICENCE: the export ships a real 1070-byte MIT LICENSE (Copyright (c) 2024 GigaChat Team), read in full rather than trusted from metadata - the Hugging Face `license` field on this repo is empty, and an earlier GigaAM v2 export shipped a file named LICENSE that was a saved GitHub web page granting nothing. WHY THIS VARIANT: the -punct export emits punctuation and normalised text, which matters when the output is typed straight into another application; the plain transducer export of the same model does not. Only the encoder is int8; decoder and joiner are full precision, as published. Needs the `sherpa` engine feature (shipped in the application since a1399a2).

entries.name: Moonshine tiny en (int8, sherpa-onnx export)
entries.description: English-only ASR designed for short utterances on small devices; int8 ONNX, no fixed 30 s padding, so cost scales with the length of what you actually said.

measurements.machine: ASUS Zenbook A16 - Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme X2E94100, 48 GB, Windows 11 build 28000 ARM64
measurements.source: `lw bench tests/fixtures/audio --model-dir <models>/moonshine-tiny-en --backend cpu`, 2026-09-18, lw-cli built with --features sherpa (sherpa-onnx 1.13.6, greedy search, 8 threads, bundled ONNX Runtime CPU provider). Word-weighted WER 0.092 and mean RTF 0.0122 over 3 clip(s) in en. ONE SWEEP: every entry in this catalog was measured back to back on the CPU on this date, over the same committed twelve-clip fixture set, so the figures are comparable with each other. The CPU is the only accelerator they can all use -- sherpa-onnx links its own static ONNX Runtime with the CPU provider, so nothing but parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 has any other path. Three clips is indicative, not statistically meaningful, and must NOT be compared with the twelve-clip multilingual totals in this catalog.

entries.notes: VERIFIED: download_bytes/disk_bytes are the exact sum of the five pinned file sizes in models/manifests/moonshine-tiny-en.json (preprocess.onnx plus the int8 encode / uncached_decode / cached_decode graphs and tokens.txt); all five SHA-256 values were computed locally on 2026-09-16 from the downloaded bytes - upstream publishes none. The MIT licence is the LICENSE file committed in the export repository (Copyright (c) 2024 Useful Sensors). SOURCE CHANGED from the earlier entry: it used to point at sherpa-onnx-moonshine-tiny-en-int8.tar.bz2 (107600538 bytes) in the `asr-models` GitHub release, but the installer cannot unpack archives, so the manifest now pins the identical loose files from the sherpa-onnx author's Hugging Face mirror at a fixed commit revision. preprocess.onnx is full precision upstream and is pinned as a common file because there is no int8 variant of it. INSTALLED AND RUN, 2026-09-16: it was installed with `lw models install moonshine-tiny-en`, which downloaded all five files and SHA-256-verified each against the committed manifest, and then benchmarked over the whole committed fixture set - see the measurement below and read its source line before quoting either number. That measurement REPLACED an earlier one-clip point (wer 0.200 on fleurs_en_1.wav alone); one measurement per model and hardware, taken the same way as every other entry here, is worth more than two that disagree because one used a third of the data. NOT VERIFIED: three English clips is a small sample, so wer_estimates is still empty; Moonshine publishes WER comparisons against Whisper tiny/base for its own checkpoints, not for this int8 ONNX export, so nothing is quoted from upstream either. The quality and speed tiers remain EDITORIAL. Needs the `sherpa` engine feature.

entries.name: SenseVoice Small (int8, sherpa-onnx export)
entries.description: Alibaba's non-autoregressive multilingual model: Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean and Cantonese in one pass, with inverse text normalisation and punctuation.
entries.notes: VERIFIED: download_bytes/disk_bytes are the exact sum of the two pinned file sizes in models/manifests/sense-voice-small.json (model.int8.onnx + tokens.txt); both SHA-256 values were computed locally on 2026-09-16 from the downloaded bytes, because upstream publishes none. SOURCE: the `asr-models` GitHub release only ships .tar.bz2 archives, which the installer cannot unpack, so the manifest pins the identical loose files from the sherpa-onnx author's Hugging Face mirror at a fixed commit revision. LICENCE - READ THIS: not an SPDX licence. The export repository's LICENSE file points at the FunASR Model Open Source License Agreement v1.1 (https://github.com/modelscope/FunASR/blob/main/MODEL_LICENSE), a custom Alibaba Group agreement which permits use, copying, modification and sharing but requires attribution and retention of model names, disclaims all liability, and terminates if you 'denigrate' the software. It is not OSI-approved and is more restrictive than the MIT/CC-BY terms of the other entries; check it before redistributing. NOT VERIFIED: no run of any kind on any machine, so no measurements. wer_estimates is empty: FunAudioLLM publishes comparisons against Whisper on AISHELL-1/Common Voice for the full-precision checkpoint, not for this int8 ONNX export, and we did not retrieve that table. The quality and speed tiers are EDITORIAL; 'very_fast' reflects that SenseVoice Small is non-autoregressive (one encoder pass, no token-by-token decode loop), not a timing. The engine string is `sense_voice`, which this build's EngineKind does not know - it round-trips as an unknown engine, which is intended for a catalog that may outlive the binary.

measurements.machine: ASUS Zenbook A16 - Snapdragon X2 Elite Extreme X2E94100, 48 GB, Windows 11 build 28000 ARM64
measurements.source: `lw bench tests/fixtures/audio --model-dir <models>/sense-voice-small --backend cpu`, 2026-09-18, lw-cli built with --features sherpa (sherpa-onnx 1.13.6, greedy search, 8 threads, bundled ONNX Runtime CPU provider). Word-weighted WER 0.062 and mean RTF 0.0141 over 3 clip(s) in en. ONE SWEEP: every entry in this catalog was measured back to back on the CPU on this date, over the same committed twelve-clip fixture set, so the figures are comparable with each other. The CPU is the only accelerator they can all use -- sherpa-onnx links its own static ONNX Runtime with the CPU provider, so nothing but parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3 has any other path. Three clips is indicative, not statistically meaningful, and must NOT be compared with the twelve-clip multilingual totals in this catalog. AND READ THIS ONE TWICE: SenseVoice covers zh/ja/ko/yue/en and the fixture set contains only the last of those, so 0.062 describes its English, which is its secondary language. This catalog holds NO measurement of the Chinese, Japanese, Korean or Cantonese it exists for.
